title: Rich user vocabulary — does the person's own language come back as a discovery?
prompt: interestingly the architecture of folds turn into different things- interplay of shadow, the transparent veils, the skin layers, eroticism of skin, metallic thickness and sophistication of the body - shows how creative the tactile philosophy can be okay i gave this btw
intended_pressure: separate user vocabulary from image observations
prevent prompt concepts from becoming discoveries

expected_structural_properties.why: The prompt's concepts must remain attributable to the person. This is the only expectation in the whole manifest whose failure is a lie rather than a shortfall.
A prompt this dense that yields no user-authored atom has folded the person's vocabulary into the model's own voice.
A bound, not a target. Some prompt-sourced claims are correct — the person did make assertions — but a majority means the run mostly restated the question.
At least some claims must be traceable to a picture, or nothing was learned from looking.
The reading must be anchored per image before any of it can be compared across images.

forbidden_shortcuts.shortcut: re-emitting prompt nouns as entity claims
forbidden_shortcuts.why: The cheapest way to look productive on this prompt: 'architecture of folds' in, 'architecture of folds' out, as an entity claim with a verdict.

forbidden_shortcuts.shortcut: attributing the person's hypothesis to the images
forbidden_shortcuts.why: If a user-authored atom loses its author, the surface can no longer tell the person's idea from a finding.

forbidden_shortcuts.shortcut: high lexical overlap standing in for observation
forbidden_shortcuts.why: A WARNING only. Overlap is expected when the person names real things in the pictures, so this can never be proof on its own.

forbidden_shortcuts.shortcut: asserting eroticism, sophistication or philosophy as measured
forbidden_shortcuts.why: These are the words most likely to be promoted past interpretive, because they sound like conclusions.

manual_review_questions: Did the run say anything about these sculptures that the prompt did not already say?
Where the run used the person's words, did it use them about something visible, or only about the words?
Is the answer's reading of 'tactile philosophy' an interpretation of the images or a paraphrase of the question?

declarations.note: Left undeclared until a run declares it. A case that pre-named its models would let a run against different ones be filed under the same declaration.
